# pve_pool (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox VE resource pool (`/pools`). PVE's create endpoint does not accept members; guest and storage members declared in `vms`/`storages` are attached (and detached) through `PUT /pools/{poolid}` after creation. Members may also join a pool at guest or storage create time; the `members` attribute is a computed view of the pool's current contents.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pve_pool" "prod" {
  poolid  = "prod"
  comment = "Production workload pool"

  vms      = [100]
  storages = ["local"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `poolid` (String) The pool identifier (PVE `pve-poolid` format). Changing this value forces recreation.

### Optional

- `allow_move` (Boolean) Allow adding a guest even if it is already in another pool; the guest is removed from its current pool and added to this one. Defaults to `false`. Also requires permission to modify the guest's current pool.
- `comment` (String) Description of the pool.
- `storages` (Set of String) Set of storage IDs that belong to the pool. Storages must exist. Removal from the set detaches the storage from the pool.
- `vms` (Set of Number) Set of guest VMIDs that belong to the pool. Guests must exist; a guest already in another pool needs `allow_move = true` to be moved into this pool. Removal from the set detaches the guest from the pool (the guest itself is untouched).

### Read-Only

- `members` (Attributes List) Current pool members, in upstream order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--members))

<a id="nestedatt--members"></a>
### Nested Schema for `members`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Member object identifier, e.g. `qemu/100` or `storage/local`.
- `node` (String) Node hosting the member object.
- `storage` (String) Storage identifier, set only for storage members.
- `type` (String) Member type. Must be one of: `qemu`, `lxc`, `openvz`, `storage`.
- `vmid` (Number) Guest VMID, set only for guest members.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing pool by its poolid.
terraform import pve_pool.prod prod
```
